title: Parseval's identity for Boolean functions
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with the uniform probability measure. Then the $L^2$ inner product of $f$ with itself equals the sum of the squares of its Fourier--Walsh coefficients over all subsets $S \subseteq [n]$:
\[
  \langle f, f\rangle \;=\; \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \hat f(S)^2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n (f : {0,1}^n → ℝ)
replaced:
The squared $L^2$ norm of $f$ equals the sum of squared Fourier coefficients:
\[
  \|f\|^2 \;=\; \langle f, f\rangle \;=\; \sum_{S\subseteq[n]} \hat f(S)^2.
\]
